chunks: From him, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning:

A man travels and passes by a dwelling of his on the way. Should he perform the salat in full or shorten it? He said: He shortens it. That is only [treated as full-residence prayer] for the dwelling which he has adopted as a watan.

key_terms.الْمَنْزِلِ: dwelling or lodging that belongs to him
key_terms.تَوَطَّنَهُ: has taken it as a watan, habitual place of residence
key_terms.يُسَافِرُ: travels; is in the state of journeying
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: shortens the salat as a traveler

ai.seo_question: If a traveler passes by a house he owns on the road, does he pray in full or shortened form?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the traveler who passes by a property or dwelling he owns during travel. The Imam عليه السلام states that he shortens the salat unless it is the dwelling he has taken as his watan, indicating that mere ownership of a منزل does not require full prayer.
